LESSON: READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 13
Topic 13.2: Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why is it important to read newspapers and magazines?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning
2. demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading helps you succeed in ENGLISH LANGUAGE. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING 13.2.1 EXTENSIVE READING: INDEPENDENT READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning

What this means
In this part you learn to read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a partner. (skill: demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning.
3. Practise this skill: demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why is it important to read newspapers and magazines?
2. How do we choose the materials we read?
3. When do we read?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read a variety of grade- appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers and magazines for lifelong learning.
5. Be able to: demonstrate independent reading of grade-appropriate digital and print texts such as newspapers, magazines and articles for information and enjoyment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
